task: Write an email to all employees at our 120-person company about open enrollment, which runs November 1 through November 15. Our dental plan changed to a new carrier, the HSA employer contribution went up to $800 for individuals, and everyone needs to actively re-select their plan or they'll be auto-enrolled in the 2025 default. Keep it skimmable with a short bulleted list of what changed.
rewrite:
ambition: A top benefits communicator opens with the action and the deadline, then states what happens if someone does nothing. They also turn each change into what it means for the reader. A new dental carrier means "check that your dentist is in network", and the HSA increase means "this is more employer money for you".

agency: The raw material is the carrier's in-network dentist directory, the broker's plan summary, and the direct link to the enrollment portal. None of these are in reach, so the email uses only the facts given. It leaves blanks for the portal link, the HR contact, and the new carrier's name, which only the sender knows.

acceleration: Lead with the deadline, using the inverted pyramid. Write a subject line that carries the action and the date. Use bold for the dates and the required action, one short bulleted list for changes, and plain language that 120 people with different benefits knowledge can read in under a minute.

accuracy: Have HR or the benefits broker check the sent-to-all draft against the carrier contract and the HSA contribution letter. The dates must appear exactly as given. Nov 15 falls on a Sunday this year, so confirm the portal's actual cutoff time with the broker before sending. Have one non-HR employee read it cold and say what they have to do.

deeper task:
Write an email from HR to all 120 employees about open enrollment, which runs November 1 through November 15. The subject line should carry the action and the deadline. Follow with a short bulleted list of what changed: the dental plan moved to a new carrier, and the HSA employer contribution rose to $800 for individuals. Under the dental bullet, add one line telling people to check that their dentist participates with the new carrier. Then give a one-line how-to-enroll with a blank for the portal link, and close with a blank for the HR contact name. Keep it skimmable, in plain language, with the dates and the required action in bold. Write the complete email, ready to send, with no notes or commentary.

answers.plain:
**Subject: Open Enrollment is Nov 1–15: Action Required**

Hi everyone,

Open enrollment runs **November 1 through November 15**. This year, you need to actively re-select your plan. If you don't, you'll be auto-enrolled in the 2025 default plan, which may not fit your needs.

**What's changed**

- **New dental carrier:** Our dental plan has moved to a new carrier. Review the plan details before you choose.
- **Higher HSA contribution:** The company's HSA contribution for individual coverage has increased to **$800**.

**What you need to do**

1. Review your plan options before November 1.
2. Log in to the enrollment portal between **November 1 and November 15**.
3. Actively select your plan, even if you want to keep your current coverage.
4. Confirm your submission.

**Deadline:** November 15. Elections can't be changed after that, except for qualifying life events.

If you have questions, reach out to [Name/HR contact] at [email/phone]. [Optional: we'll also hold Q&A sessions on [date/time].]

Thanks,
[Your name]
[Title]

---

A few things to check before sending:
- **Portal link:** I left out a link. Add one if you have it.
- **Late changes:** I included the line about changes after Nov 15 being limited to qualifying life events. Confirm that matches your plan rules, or remove it.
- **Default plan:** You said the default is the "2025" plan. If employees may be confused because the new plan year is 2026, say so explicitly.
- **HSA:** If you want, add the family-coverage contribution amount, or note that the $800 applies only to individuals.
answers.nudge:
**Subject:** Action required: Open enrollment is Nov 1-15. You must re-select your plan

**Preview text:** If you don't choose, you'll be auto-enrolled in the [2025] default.

---

Hi everyone,

Open enrollment runs **November 1 through November 15**. This year, **you need to actively re-select your plan**, even if you want to keep what you have. If you don't, you'll be automatically enrolled in the [2025] default plan, which may not match your current coverage.

**What changed**

- **New dental carrier:** Our dental plan has moved to [new carrier name]. Check that your dentist is in-network and look at the plan details before you choose.
- **Higher HSA contribution:** The company's HSA contribution for individual coverage increased to **$800**.
- **Re-selection required:** Nothing carries over automatically this year.

**What you need to do**

1. Review your options: [link to plan comparison or benefits guide]
2. Log in to [enrollment portal] and make your selections for medical, dental, vision, and HSA/FSA.
3. Submit and save your confirmation by **11:59 p.m. on November 15.**

**Dates to remember**

- **Nov 1:** Enrollment opens
- **Nov 15:** Enrollment closes. After this, changes are only allowed with a qualifying life event.

**Need help?**

- Questions about plans or enrollment: [name, email, phone]
- Live Q&A sessions: [date/time/location or video link]
- Carrier details and provider search: [link]

Please don't wait until the last day. Portals get busy and it's easy to miss a step. If you're covering dependents or have a planned procedure or ongoing prescriptions, take a few extra minutes to check that your coverage still works for you.

Thanks,
[Name]
[Title]

---

**Before you send, check these:**

1. **Plan year.** It's late October 2026, so a "2025 default" looks like it may be a typo or may mean last year's plan. I bracketed it. Confirm what the default actually is and name it, because that is the line people will worry about.
2. **Fill in the blanks.** The carrier name, portal link, contacts, and Q&A sessions are all placeholders.
3. **HSA eligibility.** The $800 applies to individual coverage. Employees will ask about family coverage, so add a line with that figure or say it's unchanged. Also say that HSA contributions only apply to HSA-eligible (HDHP) medical plans, if that's true for you.
4. **Send timing.** I'd send this around October 28-30 so people see it before enrollment opens. Send a short reminder on about Nov 8 and another on Nov 13. Target the reminders to employees who haven't completed enrollment, if your portal can report that.
5. **Dental transition.** If employees need new ID cards or have treatment in progress, add a line on when coverage with the new carrier starts and whether the old carrier handles anything in the meantime.

I can also write the reminder emails, a short Slack announcement, or a one-page FAQ.
